citeinfo.title: Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) data of wildfires in the Sky Island Mountains of the southwestern US and northern Mexico from 2011-2017

descript.abstract: This dataset is composed of 97 Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) images. Each dNBR represents a rough measure of fire-related vegetation change for wildfires (>400 ha) that occurred in the Sky Island Mountains within the Madrean Archipelago Ecoregion of the United States and Northern Mexico. These fires occurred between 2011 and 2017 and were mapped using Landsat 7 and 8 satellite imagery.
descript.purpose:
This database was created for the purpose of determining the approximate severity of wildfires in the Madrean Archipelago Ecoregion from 2011 to 2017, and analyzing the relationship between anthropogenic land uses, climate and fire severity.
This dataset has a companion dataset of the perimeters of the fires mapped for this analysis:
Villarreal, M.L., Poitras, T.B, and Conrad, C.R. Mapped fire perimeters from the Sky Island Mountains of US and Mexico: 1985-2017:U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9BB5TIO
This dataset is an update to the previous release of fire burn severities in the Sky Islands Mountains from 1985-2011:
Villarreal, M.L., and Poitras, T.B., 2018, Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) data of wildfires in the Sky Island Mountains of the southwestern US and Northern Mexico from 1985-2011: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9P3NIXR.

citeinfo.title: Mapped fire perimeters from the Sky Island Mountains of US and Mexico: 1985-2017

srcinfo.srccontr: The source contribution dataset was created for the purpose of delineating wildfire areas in order to approximate severity of wildfires in the Madrean Archipelago Ecoregion from 1985 to 2017, and analyze the relationship between anthropogenic land uses, climate and fire severity.

procstep.procdesc:
Pre- and post-fire scenes were selected using the USGS Global Visualization Viewer (GloVis). ArcGIS shapefiles containing polygons of the fire scars were uploaded into the viewer to aid with scene selection. All of the selected scenes were then loaded into ArcGIS for closer visual inspection to assess imagery with cloud cover, as cloud-free areas need only extend enough to encompass the burn scar area.
We chose pre- and post-fire images with the best possible matching anniversary dates to minimize differences in sun angle and phenology.
1) Pre-fire scenes were selected based on the closest date prior to the fire ignition. When necessary, largely due to cloud cover, pre-fire scenes were selected from a year or two before their fire ignition dates, as long as conditions were comparable and no interim disturbances overlapped the burn scar area.
2) Post-fire scenes were selected one year after the pre-fire scene date, resulting in an extended assessment one year after the occurrence of any given fire. By waiting until the following year, burned vegetation has had time to recover and demonstrate additional responses indicative of initial severity.
Of the 97 fires that we analyzed, Landsat 8 OLI images were used as much as possible for pre-fire/post-fire comparisons. If there was not a Landsat 8 OLI image available for pre-fire conditions, Landsat 7 ETM imagery was used for pre-fire and post-fire comparisons. 34 dNBR images were developed from Landsat 7 ETM data. However, due to the known "striping" issue associated with Landsat 7 ETM SLC-off data products; these images have areas of missing data that affect portions of the total burned-area.

The next step was the application of the Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) image. The dNBR highlights areas where fire has changed the spectral values between the two image dates. The pre- and post-fire images are terrain corrected and further processed to convert to surface reflectance. The Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) is computed for each date of imagery using the following formula:
((NIR - SWIR2) / (NIR + SWIR2)) = NBR
Where NIR is Band 4 for Landsat 7, and Band 5 for Landsat 8 and SWIR2 is band 7 for both Landsat 7 and 8.
The total differenced NBR is computed by subtracting the post-fire NBR from the pre-fire NBR:
(PreNBR – PostNBR) x 1000 = dNBR
Where 1000 is a conventional scaling factor applied to the dNBR.

enttyp.enttypd:
Included in this data package are 97 dNBRs, in Raster image format (.tif); created from fires that occurred between 2011-2017 within the Sky Island mountain ranges in the USA and Mexico.
Each dNBR is named for the fire that it is associated with. The naming convention for dNBRs within the US are based on the MTBS fire naming designations, and these names were not changed. MTBS (Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity) is a multiagency program which maps burn perimeters and severity of wildfires throughout the US (https://www.mtbs.gov/). The names of dNBRs within Mexico are designated according to the following protocol: Each fire is named for the Sky Island mountain complex that the fire occurs within, along with the date of the first Landsat scene showing evidence of a fire-scar. For example:"EL-PINITO-20110521", this fire took place within the El Pinito complex on or around May 21, 2011.

overview.eaover: This dataset is composed of 97 Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) images. Each dNBR represents a wildfire that occurred in the Sky Island Mountains within the Madrean Archipelago Ecoregion of the United States and Mexico. These fires occurred from 2011 to 2017 and were mapped using Landsat satellite imagery.
